title: Local Galois deformation rings and their components, Part II: explicit tame GL₂ rings of small Hodge type
summary: For a sufficiently generic semisimple two-dimensional residual representation over an unramified p-adic field, this roadmap computes framed potentially crystalline deformation rings for one tame inertial type and for the types containing a fixed Serre weight. Rank-two gauge charts and effective monodromy approximation give Hodge-labelled components, reduced special fibres and an integral component-intersection identity needed in patching. The two Hodge profiles are (3,0) and (2,1); the construction therefore extends beyond potentially Barsotti–Tate weights.
readme: The detailed mathematical plan and checks are in research/blueprint/readmes/LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartII.md. T.0–T.4 fix tame types, gauge charts, monodromy and residual labels; T.5 supplies the effective polynomial comparison; T.6–T.7 prove the one-type and several-type presentations. General deformation rings, Breuil–Kisin carriers, Serre-weight coordinates and completed commutative algebra are imported. The independent unrestricted-ring and weight-zero Emerton–Gee directions are assigned to the split proposals in the packet. All source statements are rewritten with preprint page locators.

stages.title: Tame types and their weight labels
stages.description: Construct characteristic-zero rank-two tame types and orientations, and compare their reductions with the imported Serre-weight coordinates. Establish the one-unit loss of depth and the Jordan–Hölder formula, keeping the norm-determinant twist explicit.

stages.title: Rank-two Kisin gauge charts
stages.description: On the imported Breuil–Kisin category with tame descent and coefficient change, define the rank-two eigenbasis matrices, residual shapes and gauge-basis predicate. Prove existence and uniqueness modulo the residual-trivial diagonal torus for (h+1)-generic type, and characterize the Hodge bound through minors.

stages.title: Monodromy and its finite jets
stages.description: Construct the Frobenius-compatible monodromy derivation and its regularity condition. Derive the leading matrix and finite jet equations with the actual Frobenius-coupled error terms and their explicit p-divisibility bounds.

stages.title: Residual representations and restriction
stages.description: Build the monomial étale φ-modules and their tame Galois extensions. Prove good-pair classification, the unramified-twist formula, cyclotomic-free full faithfulness on Hom, and descent of isomorphisms under 2-genericity.

stages.title: Admissible types and residual Kisin modules
stages.description: For semisimple residual rank two with a normalized N-deep presentation, N≥12, construct the three-shape family of types, the unique semisimple residual Kisin module of each shape, and the weight-to-extreme-shape bijection. Identify precisely the 2^f types containing a fixed weight after the norm-determinant twist.

stages.title: Polynomial charts and effective comparison
stages.description: Define the small-Hodge finite-union quotient of the existing fixed-profile rings. Write the three eight-variable polynomial charts, five equations and two component factors. Prove irreducibility and the p³ Jacobian bound, the chart-specific effective approximation theorem and Hodge-profile nonemptiness; obtain one ambient automorphism, equal to identity modulo p^(N−8), transporting all model equations and component ideals to the actual monodromy quotient.

stages.title: Single-type rings and their special fibres
stages.description: Specialize the existing framed potentially crystalline rings to the two Hodge profiles (3,0) and (2,1), with determinant unfixed. Prove the presentation after 2f versus four formal variables, identify all 2^f Hodge-labelled components of relative dimension f+4, and prove the normal-crossing special-fibre form and formal smoothness of each component.

stages.title: Several tame types and component intersections
stages.description: Construct the nine-variable common charts for a fixed Serre weight, transport the actual single-type ideals into them, and present the reduced flat union by an intersection of type ideals. Identify its 4^f components. Define the exact local (2,1) ideals and prove the p-membership relation with the middle-shape (3,0) ideal, retaining the global dependence of the transported tails.
